text:
incident-bot: PAGER: suspicious auth traffic + possible log leak detected on ingestion pipeline. Severity: P2. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/2123456789 :rotating_light:

james_sre: I’m on it — joining bridge now. any customer-facing errors visible?

ana_sec: Not seeing API 5xx spike. Auth logs show a burst of stale-service tokens from a handful of IPs, plus a S3 uploader job emitting verbose debug logs to the live index. suspect: misconfigured debug flag in logshipper.

maria_ops: can someone post the quick grep for token patterns? I’ll start isolating the pipeline.

raj_prod: grep run: ```grep -E "(sk_live|svcacct|token)" /var/log/ingester/* | head -n 50``` found ~30 hits across two pods, some lines include tenant IDs. don’t open to public.

james_sre: thx. Maria — please cordon the two ingestion pods and set log level to INFO immediately. Raj, list the affected tenant IDs (obfuscate customer names).

maria_ops: cordoned: ingester-7a and ingester-7b. rolling restart with LOG_LEVEL=info now.

raj_prod: affected_tenants: [t-3482, t-9921]. No PII seen, but tokens and truncated file paths present. I’m running an S3 object list to see if any debug bundles were uploaded externally.

ana_sec: action: revoke any service keys indexed in logs. I’ll create a short-run rotation plan for the affected service users. Can we rotate keys for svc-ingest role?

james_sre: yes — rotate svc-ingest keys and block the two source IPs at WAF. Maria, can you push the WAF rule?

maria_ops: WAF rule pushed: block 203.0.113.45 and 198.51.100.22. Also disabled the external uploader role in staging and prod.

ana_sec: key rotation command (run by ops): ```./scripts/rotate-service-key --role svc-ingest --scope prod --revoke-old``` Confirm after run.

maria_ops: rotation completed, old keys revoked. vault audit shows revocation entries.

legal_kate: heads up — if tenant IDs map to customer accounts, we need to prepare a notice template. No confirmed customer data exfil yet, but flagging for privacy review.

james_sre: prepping timeline. pager: can you check if any active streams to external buckets match the timestamps?

pagerbot: Checking external endpoints... 2 matches to external S3 buckets between 02:12-02:18 UTC. Buckets appear to be owned by a third-party analytics vendor; we have object PUTs with names containing "debug-dump". Flagged for retrieval and deletion request.

raj_prod: pulling the objects now, will quarantine copies in a locked bucket and provide checksums.

ana_sec: next steps: 1) preserve evidence (done by raj), 2) rotate keys (done), 3) remediate misconfig (log level) (done), 4) block IPs (done), 5) prepare customer comms if tenant mapping shows sensitive data.

james_sre: good. Maria — schedule a 30m postmortem in 2 hours and invite sec, legal, cs. Ana — please draft the initial incident summary for execs. Keep it high-level.

maria_ops: scheduled. calendar invite sent.

ana_sec: initial summary draft: "Detected anomalous auth traffic and debug log uploads from ingest pipeline. Immediate mitigations: rotated service keys, blocked suspicious IPs, reverted log verbosity. Investigating potential exposure of tenant identifiers; no confirmed PII or credentials in customer-owned storage. Further forensics in progress."

legal_kate: that wording seems fine for now. If we confirm sensitive customer secrets, we’ll need to follow the breach notification playbook.

raj_prod: quarantined objects checksums: sha256: abc123... (stored in secure evidence bucket). Full artifact list uploaded to bridge.

james_sre: outstanding: confirm whether any customer-facing requests failed during restarts, and whether any downstream caches ingested leaked tokens. Raj, run a quick token-use audit against auth logs for last 24h.

raj_prod: running audit now, will post results in 10m.

pagerbot: Pager duty escalation: on-call sec lead has been paged.

james_sre: thanks all. keep replies concise in this thread; use bridge for voice. :thumbsup:
